ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 8 November 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information issued by the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation (Order No. 3 of 2024, effective 1 November 2024); Counter-Terrorism Law of the People's Republic of China; Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024); Measures for the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Supervision and Administration of Financial Institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the founding corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent corporate registry in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the document if required by Chinese counterparties; if the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention contracting state, obtain an apostille from that state's designated competent authority and present it in China without further consular legalization. If the issuing jurisdiction is a non-contracting state, obtain authentication by the origin state's foreign ministry and then consular legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China in that origin state. The apostille and consular legalization routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of No Adverse Record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the founding shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same parallel authentication doctrine as all bundle instruments: for Apostille Convention origin, notarize if needed and affix apostille from the origin state's competent authority; for non-Apostille origin, local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by PRC consular legalization in the origin state; do not combine apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing the incorporation of the WFOE and granting Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the founding corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute under corporate seal, notarize in the jurisdiction of execution; for Apostille Convention states, apostille by that state and use directly in China; for non-member states, authenticate at the origin state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalize at the Chinese embassy or consulate in that state; the two paths are alternative and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or constitutional document of the founding corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or certified corporate secretary in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Produce a certified true copy; notarize where required; if the origin country is an Apostille Convention state, affix apostille and submit to Chinese authorities without consular legalization; if the origin country is not an Apostille Convention state, perform local MFA authentication followed by consular legalization at the PRC embassy or consulate; never chain apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the founding shareholder's principal banker
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the founding shareholder's operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issue on bank letterhead with banker's signature and, where possible, corporate seal; for Apostille Convention jurisdictions, notarize the signature and attach an apostille for acceptance in China; for non-Apostille jurisdictions, authenticate through the local government channel and then legalize at the Chinese consular post in the issuing country; the two routes are mutually exclusive and must not be concatenated.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed beneficial owners, directors, senior managers, authorized signatories, and any person owning 25% or more of the WFOE must be screened before filing against politically exposed person databases, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK sanctions lists, World Bank debarment lists, and the PRC designated terrorist financing and terrorist organization list. Each UBO must disclose source of funds and wealth and provide passport or corporate ownership chain evidence. Any positive hit requires enhanced due diligence, escalation to the AML compliance officer, suspension of formation steps if necessary, and, where mandated, submission of a suspicious transaction report to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center. A written risk assessment must be retained for at least 10 years under PRC record-keeping requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR Enterprise Name Self-Declaration Portal and National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation and local Administrations for Market Regulation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Market entity names in mainland China must be composed in simplified Chinese characters. Foreign names and phonetic transliterations may be registered only as supplementary English names and do not replace the Chinese name. The statutory four-tier name structure requires administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business characteristics, and organizational form; a WFOE must use a limited liability company organizational form suffix. Transliteration must follow standard Chinese phonetic conventions and must not be misleading, deceptive, or inconsistent with the sector or approved scope.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a formal name rejection, request a written statement of reasons from the local Administration for Market Regulation within 5 business days. Correct the rejected name by removing prohibited or sensitive tokens or by obtaining prior ministerial approval if the token is within a regulated industry. Submit a new name declaration through the SAMR name self-service portal and, if necessary, file an administrative reconsideration application with the superior administration within 60 days of the rejection, or file an administrative lawsuit with the competent People's Court within six months. Include the original rejection notice, corrected constitutional documents, and a legal brief demonstrating compliance; all appeal submissions must be in simplified Chinese and supported by translated corporate documents.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a WFOE in the deep-sea Ro-Ro vehicle transport sector. The State Administration for Market Regulation, municipal tax authorities, and PRC commercial banks uniformly reject mail-only addresses for new market entity registration. The WFOE must maintain a physical business premise in mainland China evidenced by a valid lease or ownership certificate, a physical company nameplate, utility bills, and operational substance such as personnel, communication facilities, and accounting records. A licensed serviced office may be accepted only if it provides a dedicated physical workstation and a genuine commercial presence, and the tax bureau and banks will still require lease invoices and physical inspection access.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection checklist includes: original lease agreement, landlord identity and title documents, company nameplate at the entrance, occupied working space and furniture, responsible person or employee presence, business license display, fixed telecommunication and utility receipts, accounting records kept at or accessible from the premises, and consistency between registered scope and actual activity. Quantified risk is moderate-to-high: an estimated 35% to 45% annual probability of a registry or tax bureau on-site inspection within the first 24 months for transport-sector WFOEs, increasing to approximately 90% if adverse indicators such as mail-only address, mismatched signboard, no personnel, or unrelated tenant history are identified.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory official filing fee is charged for WFOE registration; government registry fee is therefore zero.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enterprise name clearance, declaration, and availability search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation online name declaration system
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Name declaration and reservation through SAMR online portal carry no official government fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External legal counsel pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO charting, and corporate structuring
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Stage 1 WFOE formation legal work; not a statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of Articles of Association, shareholders' resolutions, board powers, and corporate consents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly fee for transactional corporate drafting.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External licensed PRC law firm and landlords
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for lease due diligence and substance verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and authentication bundle for the five mandatory corporate documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee schedules and official apostille or consular legalization fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of corporate documents into simplified Chinese and English counterpart
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation agency with registered translator seals

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance database providers and screening service firms
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial annual subscription or per-screening fee allocated to this formation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024), Articles 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 16, 23, 24, 32, 33, 34, 35, 44, 45, 47, 49, 51, 58, 59, 61 and 62; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6, 12, 13, 25, 28 and 31; Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Company Registration, Articles 1-29; Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign Investment Access (2021 Edition) as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Market Regulation Administration of the district where the WFOE is domiciled, operating through the national online enterprise registration portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application Form and the Articles of Association (company charter); upon successful registration the registry issues the Business License of a Foreign-Funded Limited Liability Company with a Unified Social Credit Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the current Company Law. A WFOE is not required to maintain a blocked escrow account or to pay in registered capital at incorporation. The sole shareholder must, however, pay the subscribed capital in full within five years from the date of incorporation unless the Articles of Association prescribe an earlier date. For international ship transportation, the Ministry of Transport licensing criteria require proof of a merchant vessel under the company's ownership or bareboat charter and financial capacity, but this is a licensing condition, not a capital escrow requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at a duly written unanimous resolution of the Board of Directors of CN WFOE LTD (the 'Company'), adopted in accordance with the Companies Law of the People's Republic of China and the Company's Articles of Association, that: 1. APPOINTMENT OF LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE. The Board appoints Mr./Ms. [Name] as Executive Director and Legal Representative of the Company, with authority to represent the Company in all dealings with government authorities, banks, courts, third parties, and service providers within the limits of the Articles of Association. 2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT. The Board approves the subscribed share capital set forth in the Articles, being RMB [amount] divided into [number] ordinary shares of RMB [par value] each. The shareholder shall subscribe and pay the capital contribution by cash or lawful contributed assets in accordance with the attached contribution schedule. Every contribution shall be made no later than five years from establishment. The Board confirms that no capital shall be reduced, returned, or loaned to the shareholder except as expressly permitted by law and subject to a lawful creditors' procedure. 3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE AND BUSINESS SCOPE. The Board adopts [Address] as the registered office and confirms that the Company's approved business scope includes deep-sea roll-on/roll-off vehicle carriage, international shipping, marine freight forwarding, and ancillary logistics services. The Legal Representative is authorized to execute the lease, to negotiate counterpart consents, and to file all required registry notices. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board designates [Bank Name], [Branch Name] as the Company's principal settlement bank. The Legal Representative and the General Manager are jointly appointed as account signatories; any transfer exceeding RMB [threshold] shall require both signatures, with a third backup signatory appointed by the Supervisor. The bank may rely upon this resolution until replaced by a subsequent board resolution. 5. STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board appoints [Name] as General Manager, [Name] as Head of Compliance and Safety Management, and [Name] as Supervisor for a term of three years. The Supervisor shall supervise the legality of financial conduct and the acts of the Legal Representative and may call interim shareholders' meetings when necessary. 6. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the General Manager, in the name of the Company, to prepare, execute, submit, and pursue all applications, filings, declarations, licenses, contracts, and undertakings required for opening the company, and to retain lawyers, accountants, agents, and consultants. Any instrument signed by the Legal Representative or the General Manager under the Company seal shall be binding on the Company. This resolution takes immediate effect and may be produced as a certified extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foreign Investor Identity Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Online Enterprise Registration Platform and the local Market Regulation Administration of the intended domicile.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed English and Chinese trade name through the integrated enterprise registration and name reservation system. Before reservation, verify the business scope against the Foreign Investment Negative List to ensure that deep-sea Ro-Ro shipping is not in the restricted or prohibited category. The foreign investor, whether individual or corporate, must pass the automated identity verification procedure; a legal entity investor shall provide an apostilled or consularly legalized certificate of incorporation and a certified Chinese translation. The system will issue a Name Reservation Notice valid for six months. Review any conflicts, print the notice, and retain the tracking reference for the formal filing.
required_dossiers: Notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation of the foreign shareholder or passport of the individual shareholder
Power of attorney appointing the local filing agent
Proposed company name in Chinese and English
Business scope description referencing ISIC 5012 and NAICS 483111
Foreign-invested entity Negative List compliance statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name or scope is rejected, the applicant shall modify and resubmit within five working days; if the rejection is based on a Negative List misinterpretation, the filer may submit an explanatory memorandum and require issuance of a written refusal, after which administrative reconsideration may be filed with the next-higher SAMR within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Constitutional Documents and Share Capital Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foreign investor and the Chinese notary public if local practice requires notarization; the local SAMR for document recataloging.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name reservation, the sole shareholder must execute the Articles of Association, a written shareholder decision, and a capital subscription schedule. The articles shall set out the name, registered address, business scope, subscribed capital, legal representative, board structure, supervisor, and contribution period. Since this is a wholly foreign-owned limited company, a single written shareholder decision may be used instead of a shareholders' meeting. The foreign investor shall verify that all signatures correspond to the identity instruments submitted in step one. Under Chinese conflict-of-laws practice, the governing law clause shall refer to the Companies Law of the PRC. If the registered office is leased, attach the landlord's title certificate and valid lease; if the landlord is a state-owned enterprise, obtain the state-asset approval document. The constitutional package is filed later, but it is certified now to avoid procedural delay.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association in Chinese
Written decision of sole shareholder on incorporation and capital subscription
Capital contribution schedule with deadlines
Identity instruments of all directors, supervisor, and legal representative
Leased premises ownership certificate and lease agreement
Foreign Investment Law compliance statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is challenged, the foreign shareholder can sign in front of the Chinese consulate or use apostille under the Hague Convention; if the content is non-compliant, the local SAMR guidance office can issue a correction sheet, to be cured within ten working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Approval of Establishment Registration and Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration under SAMR, through the integrated online one-stop government service window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the full establishment registration through the SAMR integrated platform or the one-stop government service window. The official state fee is nil for company registration under current fee waiver policy, but stamp tax on paid-in capital and capital books may arise later. The filing bundle must include the name reservation notice, constitutional documents, proof of registered address, appointment instruments of the legal representative and supervisor, and the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Form. The registry will check all names, legal representative qualifications, Negative List compliance, and the validity of the address proof. After review, SAMR publishes the Unified Social Credit Code, issues the electronic and paper business license, and generates the enterprise information receipt. The applicant then applies to a licensed engraving firm for the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal. This stage closes with the official seal record card.
required_dossiers: Application for Establishment Registration signed by the legal representative
Name Reservation Approval Notice
Articles of Association and share subscription decision
Lease and building title proof
Director, supervisor, and legal representative appointment documents and identity copies
Foreign Investment Information Reporting Form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where SAMR issues a rectification demand, the filer shall submit corrected electronic copies within 15 working days; if approval is withheld, the filer may request a written denial and apply for administrative review or file an administrative suit within six months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Multi-Registration for Tax, Social Insurance, Housing Fund and Statistics
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration provincial E-Tax Bureau, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, and Housing Provident Fund Management Center.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is granted, the Unified Social Credit Code is automatically transmitted by SAMR through the one-stop data sharing mechanism to the tax authority, customs authority, and statistics office. The company's legal representative must log in to the electronic tax bureau within 30 days and complete tax status confirmation. During tax registration, the company selects VAT payer type, establishes payroll records for employees, and connects the bank account for automatic financial reporting. Social insurance and housing fund obligations arise only when the first employee is hired; nonetheless, the company must open an employer account in advance and record the office address for labor inspector communications. The finance department must compute stamp tax on the Articles and paid-in capital and file returns even if the amount is zero. Any foreign employee's work and residence clearance is handled separately with the Exit-Entry Administration.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Legal representative identity certificate
Articles of Association
Bank account details or capital account opening certificate
Payroll and social insurance employer registration form
Financial institution information for tax collection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority identifies an inconsistency, the filer must respond via the E-Tax portal within 15 working days with an explanation and revised forms; a failure to respond may cause automatic suspension of invoice issuance. Administrative reconsideration before the STA may follow an unfavorable determination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Bank Accounts, SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Chinese commercial bank with foreign exchange operations and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through its authorized bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a basic deposit account and, if needed, a foreign currency capital account with a licensed bank branch. The legal representative must appear in person with the business license, official seals, and board resolution, or present a notarized power of attorney if absent. The bank will carry out know-your-customer and beneficial owner verification. Through delegated foreign exchange registration, the bank submits the foreign direct investment information to SAFE's digital system. The legal representative will supply a declaration that the subscribed capital will only be used for the approved business scope. If the shareholder transfers capital from overseas, the bank will monitor the purpose and record the capital account matter. No escrow account is required, but the bank may impose an internal threshold approval for large transfers. After all signatures are captured, bank seals are stamped on the account opening application, and online banking tokens are issued.
required_dossiers: Business License and filing certificate
Original Articles of Association
Board resolution authorizing bank signatories
Company seal, financial seal, and legal representative seal
Passport or identity documents of representatives and beneficial owner
Lease contract or proof of business address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects or queries the application, the bank shall provide a written reason; the applicant may amend the board resolution or KYC package and reapply at the same or another bank. A supervisory complaint may be filed with the local branch of the People's Bank of China if the refusal is unjustified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Maritime Operating Licenses, Vessel Registration and Safety Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Transport, Department of Water Transport; Maritime Safety Administration of the port of vessel registration; and the local Municipal Port Administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the WFOE obtains its business license and bank account, submit to the Ministry of Transport an application for the International Maritime Vessel Operation Permit. The application shall prove that the company is lawfully established, that its business scope includes international marine transport, and that it has a seaworthy Ro-Ro vessel owned, co-owned, or chartered on a bareboat basis for the intended routes. The operator must submit a Safety Management System under the ISM Code, vessel insurance covering P&I liability, a ship security plan under ISPS, and crew certificates satisfying STCW requirements. The authority inspects technical condition, tonnage, manning, route, and the company's shore management. Once the permit and vessel registration certificate are granted, the vessel applies for radio and safety certificates, and the company files each voyage with the port authority before first sailing. Revocation risks include failure to sail within a specified period or material changes in ownership.
required_dossiers: WFOE Business License and Articles of Association
International Maritime Vessel Operation Permit application form
Ship ownership or bareboat charter certificate
Safety Management Certificate or Interim Safety Management Certificate
Classification society certificates for hull and machinery
Crew nationality and STCW certification list
International Ship Security Certificate application and ship security plan
Protection and indemnity insurance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Transport raises queries, the operator shall provide supplemental technical evidence within 20 working days; if denied, it may request a written decision and initiate administrative reconsideration within 60 days or administrative litigation within six months. Temporary suspension can be cured by updating the safety management system and passing re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Transport, Department of Water Transport; Maritime Safety Administration of China; and the local Municipal Port Administration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Maritime Vessel Operation Permit issued under the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on International Maritime Transportation; Vessel Registration Certificate; Safety Management Certificate; International Ship Security Certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China (MEE), as applied by port and maritime authorities; vessel-source emissions are additionally governed by the Maritime Safety Administration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable for the mobile vessel itself; no full Environmental Impact Assessment report is required for the WFOE shore office unless it constructs a terminal, warehouse, or shore power facility. The Ro-Ro vessel operation is subject to international ship-source pollution prevention rather than land-based EIA categorization.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: MARPOL 73/78 standards as adopted by China: oily water effluent must contain less than 15 parts per million oil before prohibited discharge beyond 12 nautical miles; sulfur content of marine fuel oil must not exceed 0.50% m/m and must not exceed 0.10% m/m inside Chinese Domestic Emission Control Areas when at berth or during certain operations; nitrogen oxide emissions must not exceed IMO NOx Tier II or Tier III limits depending on keel-laying date; ballast water management must comply with the Ballast Water Management Convention D-2 standard; all hazardous wastes, bilge slops, and waste oil must be delivered to licensed disposal facilities and recorded in the Oil Record Book, Garbage Record Book, and Solid Waste Manifest System.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance is required for the shore office as a simple civil defense filing with the Fire and Rescue Department. For the vessel, a SOLAS Cargo Ship Safety Construction Certificate and Cargo Ship Safety Equipment Certificate must be issued by the classification society or flag authority. Occupational clearance requires each seafarer to hold a valid STCW certificate of competency, a medical fitness certificate, and a seafarer's employment agreement approved under the Maritime Labour Convention; company safety management plans must be certified under the ISM Code, and the port authority may perform port state control inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online electronic portals: STA Online Tax Service Platform and the National Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice Service Platform
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the WFOE, tax registration is the standard domestic entity registration because the WFOE is a Chinese-resident limited liability company. 1. Incorporate at the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) to obtain the business license embedding the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which functions as the national taxpayer identification number. 2. Complete electronic tax registration with the competent local STA office within 30 calendar days of business license issuance via the STA Online Tax Service Platform; the USCC is activated as the Enterprise Income Tax, VAT, and customs taxpayer ID. 3. Register as a foreign-trade operator with the General Administration of Customs (GAC) to obtain the Customs Registration Code for export declarations and zero-rated export/refund processing. 4. Determine VAT status: small-scale taxpayer for expected annual taxable sales not exceeding RMB 5,000,000, or general VAT taxpayer status for cross-border input-credit efficiency, with optional voluntary registration. 5. Complete the Export Tax Refund/Exemption filing recordal within the STA online system before the first export voyage. 6. Open a foreign-currency receipts account with a licensed bank and arrange issuance of the Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) for export proceeds. Foreign non-resident entities without a Chinese permanent establishment would separately register under the STA non-resident taxpayer registration module for withholding purposes; this is distinct from the WFOE's domestic USCC tax identity. Required documentary support: foreign investor incorporation certificate, passport/corporate identity documents, articles of association, registered office lease, legal representative ID, board resolution, and maritime transport license where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the WFOE is a Chinese tax-resident limited liability company taxed at entity level on worldwide income under the Enterprise Income Tax Law; no pass-through or direct-receipt preference; qualifying Free Trade Port or encouraged-industry enterprises may access preferential CIT rates (e.g., 15%) while remaining entity-level taxpayers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity-classification pass-through; mainland China does not provide check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections. Administrative elections available: small-scale vs. general VAT taxpayer registration, simplified VAT collection for certain service categories, and export tax refund/zero-rating filing status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) of the People's Republic of China; administered by STA with import VAT collected by GAC; standard goods rate 13%, domestic transportation services rate 9%, and international ocean transport of goods qualifies for the zero rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All entities with taxable business activities must complete VAT taxpayer registration upon incorporation. Annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 generally mandate general VAT taxpayer registration; entities at or below that threshold remain small-scale taxpayers unless voluntary general registration is elected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates Golden Tax Project Phase IV through the National Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice Service Platform; taxpayers must issue fully digitalized electronic invoices with STA-controlled invoice numbers, transmit invoice data in near real-time to STA systems, and use the official tax digital account for reconciliation. System-to-system (API) integration is available only through STA-approved electronic invoice platform channels. Anti-fraud controls include real-time digital stamping, unified invoice code and QR, automatic comparison of invoices against customs declaration data, and post-issuance verification by the VAT Invoice Check System.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: International ocean RoRo carriage is zero-rated as an international transportation service under the PRC VAT regime. Eligibility requires: (1) the voyage involves carriage of cargo between a PRC port and a foreign port, or solely between foreign ports; (2) the supplier holds the statutory international water transport license; (3) the service is actually exported, i.e., the cargo is shipped under a customs export declaration and consigned to a non-PRC party; (4) the consideration is received in foreign currency from non-resident customers; (5) the entity has completed VAT zero-rate/export refund filing with STA; and (6) all supporting customs, transport, and bank documentation is retained for audit. Qualifying offshore digital services, if any separate scope, must demonstrate foreign consumption and payment from non-resident counterparties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-exchange collection receipt
International Water Transport Permit / business registration certificate
Contract of carriage or charter party
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: STA and GAC may jointly audit zero-rated export transactions. Failure to produce customs clearance evidence, valid bill of lading, FIRC, or proof of foreign-currency repatriation within 180 days triggers reclassification as a domestic taxable supply, retroactive VAT at 9% or applicable rate, late-payment surcharge at 0.05% per day, and a penalty range of 50% to five times the tax underpaid pursuant to the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. Fraudulent zero-rating, false export documents, or fake invoices further expose the WFOE to denial of refund, clawback of any refunded input VAT, customs fines, public blacklisting, and criminal liability for tax evasion or export-tax-refund fraud under PRC criminal law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), exercising foreign exchange control through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime under which the RMB is convertible for current account transactions but subject to approval and registration on the capital account. Foreign exchange for genuine trade, charter hire, bunker payments, port disbursements, and service fees may settle freely through designated commercial banks, but capital injections, cross-border loans, equity transfers, and outbound investments require SAFE registration or bank verification. Current account convertibility supports regular payments for the operation of deep-sea Ro-Ro vessel transport. Profit remittance is permitted once audited financial statements, a valid tax clearance certificate, board resolutions, and the underlying dividend distribution documents are presented; banks perform end-beneficiary review and may request a declaration of the true purpose. Retained earnings cannot be remitted before corporate income tax liabilities are settled. Capital account items such as foreign shareholder loans, cross-border guarantees, and equity disposal remain closely controlled. There is no general forced foreign exchange surrender for exporters, but export proceeds must be repatriated to China and either retained in a foreign currency account or converted at a market-quoted rate. Non-compliance with SAFE reporting requirements can trigger penalties, downgrade of banking facilities, and loss of operational approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts for ocean Ro-Ro transportation services and related vehicle export proceeds must be repatriated into a domestic designated foreign exchange bank account within 180 days from the date of export settlement, unless an extension is approved by SAFE. There is currently no mandatory conversion ratio; the statutory minimum conversion requirement is effectively 0 percent, meaning export proceeds may be held in foreign currency or voluntarily sold to the designated bank at the prevailing market rate, subject to SAFE monitoring and reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Settlement Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Settlement Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital electronic money institutions have a Low feasibility rating for serving a mainland China WFOE in a direct clearing or custody capacity. Under the PRC Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations and PBOC licensing rules, only SAFE-designated commercial banks may operate onshore foreign exchange settlement, RMB clearing, and cross-border trade payment processing for resident entities. Offshore EMIs are not authorized to open renminbi or foreign currency accounts for WFOEs, nor may they legally act as the receiving bank for export proceeds. Their role is limited to providing software-driven payment instruction, reconciliation, and distribution functionalities while all clearing and foreign exchange execution must be routed through a licensed domestic tier-one bank. Using a fintech EMI as the primary transaction account would constitute unlicensed cross-border financial activity in China and would breach SAFE reporting obligations. Therefore, the WFOE treasury structure must place domestic bank accounts at the centre and may optionally engage an EMI only as a front-end payment interface.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a wholly foreign-owned enterprise in mainland China, the legal representative or the senior authorized manager of the WFOE is generally required to appear physically at the bank branch during corporate account opening interviews. Remote consular proxy account opening is not widely accepted by major Chinese banks for domestic operational accounts. If the foreign statutory director is unable to attend in person, a locally appointed general manager or finance director may complete the interview after presenting a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, the original foreign resolution of the board of directors, passport or residence permit copies, and the WFOE business license. Some banks may permit a supplementary online video interview, but this is treated as an exception rather than a standard mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by a multi-jurisdiction offshore shareholding chain typical of shipping group treasury structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified corporate chart showing each intermediate holding company, full legal name and jurisdiction, direct and indirect ownership percentages, individual ultimate beneficial owner passport copies, overseas corporate registry extracts not older than three months, source of funds declarations, and a board resolution approving the WFOE incorporation and bank account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags from Ro-Ro vehicle transportation invoices, freight payments, and charter hire settlements with possible over- or under-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts and charter party agreements, itemized freight invoices, original bills of lading, customs export declarations, port call operational records, vessel log summaries, proof of actual deck capacity usage, audited financial statements, and a third-party verification report from the vessel commercial manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export controls exposure because ocean car carriers may have called at high-risk or restricted ports, or may be controlled by flagged entities under selective U.S., EU, or UN measures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A comprehensive adverse media search, screening of all vessel IMO numbers against OFAC, UN, EU, and PRC sanctions lists, historical AIS voyage data, port call certificates, flag state registry certificates, shipping register confirmation, insurance certificates proof that the vessel is not designated, and a sworn statement identifying all charterers and beneficial cargo owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth mismatch where the initial capital injection appears disproportionate to the commercial shipping operating revenue forecast, raising currency smuggling or money laundering concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder bank statements showing the source of funds, signed share subscription agreement, audited group financial statements for three years, a project finance business plan covering vessel charter costs and route margin projections, WFOE cash flow forecast, tax identification number certificates, and confirmation from a Chinese certified public accountant of the planned capital contribution schedule.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital for the WFOE must be paid through an FDI foreign exchange capital account opened with a designated SAFE-approved domestic bank. Before receipt, the WFOE must complete foreign direct investment registration through the SAFE or the local authorized bank, and then obtain a capital account foreign exchange business registration. The overseas shareholder transmits the funds via SWIFT wire transfer with a declared investment purpose code, usually structured as a foreign direct investment equity injection. Upon receipt, the bank performs name screening, sanctions checks, and comparison against the SAFE-registered investment amount. The funds are then converted into renminbi in a capital settlement account only after a valid capital verification report is issued by a licensed Chinese public accounting firm. No merger, acquisition, or asset acquisition from third parties is allowed without a special SAFE/FIUTS registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for Ro-Ro vessel operations, charter hire, bunker fuel, port charges, crew wages, and overseas vehicle terminal fees are cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers with proper purpose-of-payment codes and supporting shipping documents. For large supplier or shipyard payments, a commercial irrevocable letter of credit is recommended, especially where the beneficiary is a foreign shipowner, shipbuilder, or terminal operator, because it reduces counterparty risk and provides documentary discipline through presentation of original transport and commercial documents. Documentary collections may be used for lower-value and recurring trade settlements when both parties have established payment history. All outbound transactions must be reported through the SAFE banking system, and any foreign exchange payment above the statutory threshold requires a trade-in fair copy declaration and the original invoice, contract, or relevant shipping document.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB forward contracts allowed through SAFE-designated commercial banks for hedging genuine current account and approved capital account exposures, with mandatory real transaction background documents and no speculative open positions.

Cross-currency swaps permitted for matching WFOE foreign-currency debt, shareholder loans, or long-term trade receivables where the underlying exposure is supported by signed contracts and board-approved treasury policy.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards may be executed by the overseas group treasury only for portfolio-level hedge consolidation; they cannot be booked directly by the mainland WFOE as onshore derivatives without a valid SAFE/PBOC derivative qualification and underlying trade documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statement Audit and Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting / board of directors; audited report retained in the statutory books at the registered office and available for SAMR, STA, MOFCOM and SAFE inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the December 31 fiscal year-end (by April 30 of the following year), before approval of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unaudited annual financial report cannot be lawfully approved; the WFOE and the relevant officer may be fined under the PRC Company Law and Accounting Law, the company may be flagged in the SAMR credit system, and the local tax authority may reject the unaudited accounts as support for the annual final settlement, causing surcharges and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Final Settlement and Payment (Annual Reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the competent local tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing and payment due by May 31 of the immediately following fiscal year-end (December 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest accrues at 0.05% per day on the unpaid balance; fraudulent or negligent under-declaration attracts a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax; late filing attracts procedural fines up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases; continued non-payment triggers enforced collection, exit restriction, and tax credit blacklisting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report (Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each calendar year, reporting information as of December 31 of the prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by June 30 results in inclusion in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 10 working days; if the delinquency remains uncorrected for more than 3 years, inclusion in the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises, entry into the administrative deregistration/strike-off track, and joint credit restrictions on the legal representative and management.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Investment Information Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the SAMR-run National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOFCOM issues a rectification order allowing 20 days to correct; failure to correct triggers an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 300,000 on the enterprise and RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000 on directly responsible personnel, plus credit-system enforcement and possible foreign exchange restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SAFE Foreign Direct Investment Annual Stock and Equity (FDI) Registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through designated foreign-exchange banks
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to complete the annual FDI stock/equity registration by June 30 triggers a SAFE investigation, suspension or restriction of capital-account foreign-exchange transactions and repatriation, inability to complete cross-border dividend or capital redemptions, and administrative penalties under PRC foreign-exchange regulations until corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Annual Reconfirmation and 30-Day Change Notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the consolidated market-subject registration and annual credit reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual reconfirmation embedded in the January 1 - June 30 annual report cycle; any equity transfer or UBO change must be reported within 30 calendar days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False, incomplete, or late UBO filings expose the company to administrative penalties up to RMB 20,000 and responsible persons up to RMB 5,000 under the Administrative Measures for Beneficial Ownership Information of Market Entities; unregistered share transfers may also be unenforceable against bona fide third parties and result in SAMR abnormal-operation marking.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ro-Ro Ocean Shipping License and Safety Management Certificate (DOC) Annual Verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Transport (MOT) through the Maritime Safety Administration (MSA) and Recognized Organization (classification society)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: DOC annual verification by the anniversary date of each Safety Management Certificate; vessel class and statutory surveys per the triennial/annual survey schedule set by the classification society
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operation without a valid DOC or vessel certificates subjects the Ro-Ro vessel to port-state detention, prohibition from leaving PRC ports, suspension of the company's shipping license, and administrative fines; continued breach can lead to revocation of the ocean shipping license and deregistration/strike-off of the WFOE.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: There is no size-based exemption for a WFOE: under the PRC Company Law every company, including a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company, must have its annual financial statements independently audited by a licensed Chinese CPA firm. For supplementary accounting-framework classification only, a small enterprise is generally regarded as having total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million, annual operating revenue not exceeding RMB 50 million, and headcount not exceeding 300; however, even if all three quantitative thresholds are satisfied, the WFOE audit obligation remains mandatory. Any enterprise exceeding any of those thresholds is a large-or-medium enterprise required to apply full ASBE and carries a correspondingly deeper audit scope.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBEs), substantially converged with IFRS; qualified small enterprises may apply the PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards; statutory standalone accounts are prepared in RMB; IFRS is not accepted by PRC authorities as the sole statutory framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must identify every natural-person beneficial owner holding 25% or more of equity/control and must register that information with SAMR upon formation. Any change, including a direct or indirect shareholding transfer,

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Enterprise Income Tax Law, Article 4; no separate national/local corporate income tax for ordinary enterprises)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A PRC WFOE engaged in international RoRo shipping is a resident taxpayer. Incentives include: (i) a 15% reduced rate for High and New Technology Enterprises, if qualifying; (ii) an effective 5% rate for Small Low-Profit Enterprises within statutory thresholds during the applicable preferential period; (iii) an additional 100% super-deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure; (iv) the Tonnage Tax Regime permitted for international shipping enterprises, whereby qualified deep-sea shipping income may be exempt from corporate income tax and replaced by a tonnage-based levy if the enterprise meets eligibility and approval conditions; and (v) in certain free-trade zones and the Hainan Free Trade Port, a 15% preferential rate may apply to encouraged industries.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Principal return: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return (Form A), denoted in the official schedule family as A100000 and the principal corporate income tax table. Supplementary compulsory annual schedules include the entity profile table, the general tax-base adjustment schedule A105000, and the annual related-party transactions report A109000. Filing is mandatory through the electronic e-Taxation service of the State Taxation Administration; paper filing is accepted only where an exemption from e-filing is expressly granted.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement filing, with quarterly or monthly provisional (pre-payment) filings during the tax year. Foreign-invested WFOEs with a calendar-year tax year make provisional payments by the 15th day after the end of each quarter and file the annual return no later than May 31 of the following year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is due within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year. For a December 31 fiscal-year WFOE, the statutory deadline is May 31 of the next calendar year. Provisional quarterly payments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter (April 15, July 15, October 15 and January 15 respectively for calendar-year taxpayers). Where precise assessment is impossible, prior-year tax may be used as the provisional basis with approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue from the principal shipping activity, including deep-sea RoRo vehicle transshipment and related loading/lashing revenue collected as a single freight service.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Chinese resident WFOE, worldwide freight income is reported here; inbound and outbound RoRo income cannot be omitted simply because the counterparty or vessel registry is non-resident. Back-to-back arrangements with overseas affiliates should be recharacterized as principal revenue if the WFOE controls vessel capacity and bears freight risk. A Tonnage Tax election, if available, does not eliminate the need to disclose gross revenue in the reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to shipping revenue: vessel fuel and voyage costs, crew wages and social insurance, port dues, stevedoring and lashing subcontract costs, charter hire, insurance, and depreciation of owned RoRo vessels.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party charter hire and terminal services from non-resident group companies must satisfy the arm's length principle. Lack of contemporaneous documentation may lead to disallowance or deemed pricing. Costs attributable to tax-exempt Tonnage Tax income must be appropriately apportioned.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Lines 4-6 (Selling, Administrative and Financial Expenses equivalent)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Period expenses including overheads, dispatcher and administrative personnel costs, bank charges, loan interest and foreign exchange losses not capitalized.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to an offshore head office are deductible only if the services were actually performed, were not duplicated by local services, and the fee is supported by transfer pricing documentation. A non-resident parent may not charge royalties for brand or technical assistance without a valid license and DTA withholding; disguised shareholder financing may be recharacterized as dividends under thin capitalization rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciling accounting profit to taxable income: nondeductible expenditures, fines, excess entertainment, impairment provisions, related-party transfer pricing adjustments, tax-exempt income and additional deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Failure to attach the tax adjustment schedule invites automatic desk adjustments. Where the tax authority makes a transfer pricing adjustment, the additional taxable income is included in this block. Non-resident parent charges that lack documentary evidence are disallowed. Any reduction for overseas head-office overhead must comply with the Enterprise Income Tax Law implementing rules; no blanket or arbitrary apportionment is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Lines 20-23 (Taxable Income, Tax Rate and Computed Tax Amount equivalent)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of taxable income after loss carryforward, the applicable CIT rate (normally 25%, or preferential 15% if qualified), and the gross annual tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders do not file this return; the WFOE is a resident enterprise and must compute tax on worldwide income. The headline 25% cannot be unilaterally reduced by reference to the parent's tax residence. A DTA does not cap the enterprise's ordinary CIT; it applies only to outbound withholding tax charges described at Box 6.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Lines 31-32 (Foreign Tax Credit, Withholding Tax, Prepayments and Balance Due equivalent)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits for foreign income tax paid on overseas profits, deduction of provisional payments, and determination of final CIT balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE itself earns foreign-source RoRo profits and pays foreign income tax in the flag or port state, credit is limited to Chinese tax attributable to that foreign-source income. Separately, if the WFOE remits dividends, interest or royalties to a non-resident, those outbound payments are subject to withholding tax and are declared on a withholding return, not as a deduction here. Treaty relief on outbound remittances must be substantiated by the foreign payee, not claimed as a credit by the WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Lines 36-38 (Related-Party Transaction Disclosure and Special Warning Area)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual related-party transaction report and disclosure of loans, pricing, shareholding and service arrangements with overseas affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE ocean carrier with cross-border charter or management transactions must complete Form A109000 and related tables if transactions exceed notification thresholds. Deliberate omission is an indicator of deliberate evasion and may trigger a special tax investigation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is subject to the Tax Administration Law: a fine from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 (Article 62), plus a late-payment interest surcharge of 0.05% per calendar day on any unpaid tax (Article 32). Where underpayment is caused by fraudulent concealment or false returns, the authority will pursue unpaid tax and interest and impose a monetary penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax (Article 63). Failure of a withholding agent to remit withholding tax exposes a penalty of 50% to 300% (Article 69). Intentional underpayment over statutory thresholds gives rise to criminal tax evasion liability under Article 201 of the Criminal Law, with fines and imprisonment, in serious cases up to seven years. Taxpayers also face tax blacklisting, cross-system enforcement with Customs and SAFE, and exit-control restrictions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10%, imposed on the gross amount of dividends paid by the PRC WFOE to its non-resident enterprise shareholder, under Articles 3(3), 27 and 37 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law. An effective rate lower than 10% may apply only where an applicable Double Taxation Agreement reduces the rate (commonly 5% for a beneficial owner directly holding at least 25% of the voting capital; certain treaties provide other rates; no treaty reduction is automatic).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before remittance, the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the PRC withholding agent: (i) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction for the year of payment; (ii) a complete non-resident tax treaty benefit declaration through the Chinese e-Taxation system, including the commercial registration and shareholding chain; (iii) a Beneficial Ownership declaration and supporting substance evidence showing real activity, economic risk-bearing and no conduit status; and (iv) a dividend payment resolution and financial statements confirming after-tax distributable profits. The withholding agent must assess the application and withhold at the treaty-reduced rate only after the tax authority screen; otherwise statutory 10% is withheld and the foreign shareholder may apply for refund or credit within three years. A valid TRC and substance evidence are mandatory; treaty shopping through a look-through entity will be rejected.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on interest paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise is 10% of gross interest. Royalties paid to non-resident enterprises for the use of, or right to use, intellectual property in China are likewise subject to 10% WHT. Under treaty, interest is generally capped at 10%, but may be 5% or 7% under specific agreements; royalties are usually capped at 10% but many treaties provide 5% or 7%. Royalties sourced to offshore arrangements may also be subject to VAT and surcharges; the WHT field excludes VAT for the avoidance of doubt. Payments of freight income to a non-resident vessel owner may be subject to special deemed-profit taxation, with treaty exemption commonly available for international shipping under the shipping article; the WFOE should obtain treaty filings in that case.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: preparation is mandatory when a related-party transaction category exceeds RMB 200 million for tangible goods (including physical vehicle purchase or transshipment flows), RMB 100 million for financial assets, RMB 100 million for intangible assets, or RMB 40 million for other related-party
